story.head: Penalties could cost the Blue Jackets
paras: The Stars won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Dallas on Saturday. The Blue Jackets (6-7-0) beat Colorado 7-2 on Tuesday, and the Stars have won two in a row. Going in, the Stars are third in the Central (tied for 12th in the NHL) and the Jackets sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th).
This season, the Stars have outscored teams 43-35, but only 28-25 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 9-5, and no team creates more chances on the power play.

The Stars play slow, tight games (lowest) and have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st). They also block more shots than anyone (1st), so the Stars are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Blue Jackets’ shots. Dallas has allowed 2.33 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (5th) and keep things calm after the whistle (5th lowest). They also have a leaky penalty kill (29th), so the Stars’ power play (1st) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded.

Mikko Rantanen (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 15 GP) is tied for the Stars’ scoring lead. Jason Robertson (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 15 GP) shares it, with seven points in his last five games. Kent Johnson (7 G / 6 A / 13 P in 13 GP) is tied for the Blue Jackets’ scoring lead, with eight points in his last five games. Charlie Coyle (3 G / 10 A / 13 P in 13 GP) shares it.
Casey DeSmith (1-2-0 / .887 SV% in 3 GS) is expected to start for Dallas, and Cam Talbot (4-2-0 / .899 SV% in 6 GS) for Columbus.
At home, Rick Bowness likes to send Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Johnston, Benn and Rantanen.
